stages: ideal wallet with HTTPS and forced receiver shutdown

verification.scope: Final cleanup fix: forced receiver termination and observed exit; HTTPS acknowledgment loss/restart/retry.

verification.mode: Pinned real v2, current HTTPS runtime and CLI

walletAcceptance: Issue 10, request/pay 7, verify receipt and checkpoint inclusion, fulfill one local invoice; retained payer change 3 stays private and survives restart.
Receiver burns 7 and payer burns 3 in separate fresh wallet processes; verified final issued 10, burned 10, outstanding 0.
Accepted HTTP reply is deliberately dropped; restart and exact retry retain the original authenticated receipt bytes.
Re-prove the same payment with the pinned real prover: different valid proof bytes yield the same prior receipt, which still attests only the original proof.
Withheld history returns unavailable without fulfillment; duplicate invoice fulfillment is refused.
Witness paths use only verified prefix events; an appended unverified tail cannot change the proof anchor.
Exact preparation retains its saved proof; a changed recipient request is rejected against authenticated fixture pairing.
A second spend/burn preparation of the already-spent receiver input is rejected against verified history.
Service request frames contain only public statement bytes; delivery contains only receiver opening, statement and receipt, excluding payer change.
Real alternate valid proof with the original receipt is rejected before inbox storage; original receipt-attested delivery then succeeds.
Receiver HTTPS process commits before dropping its acknowledgment; restart retains the invoice capability and exact delivery, and exact retries return the same frame hash without fulfillment.
Private payer delivery never uses the former shared delivery file. Operator requests contain neither private openings nor invoice capability.
A noncooperating fixture receiver is forcibly terminated and exit is observed; independent cleanup runs after failures.

publicAudit.process: Separate process receives public evidence files, compiled public circuits and a separately supplied exact expected commitment; no wallet database or opening input.
checks: Valid payment and final burn checkpoints derive public supply totals.
Alternate independently verified real spend proof changes only the padding nullifier, preserving outputs and totals, but cannot replace the expected exact history.

crashAcceptance.boundary: Test-only interception of DatabaseSync.exec around the actual COMMIT; process.exit(71) before or after, no graceful close.
assertions: Before COMMIT recovers prior state; after COMMIT retains exact bytes.
Request secret/counter replay remains stable without reusing freshness for another request.
Pending proof, both openings and both input reservations recover together.
Original receipt survives retry and callback-return mutation.
Fulfillment retains its original checkpoint/receipt and one row across fresh-process replay.
Capability commits are stable after restart; interrupted uncommitted capability is unauthorized and replaced by fresh randomness.
Inbox commit is absent before or exact after interruption; repeated delivery returns the same hash and never records fulfillment.
crashAcceptance.timeout: Each child must reach its deliberate exit rather than a timeout; each recovery must exit successfully.

review.type: Independent adversarial design and actual source/diff review, focused execution and critical fix readback
review.choice: Use standard HTTPS with a durable invoice capability and immutable canonical inbox; original receipt attestation prevents altered-proof poisoning; fulfillment remains separate.
review.specification: Pinned pool-v2 sections 3 and 9 already provide the private delivery and receipt relations. No normative, circuit or signed-frame amendment.
resolvedFindings: UTF-8 decoding silently removed a BOM. Preserve it so canonical reconstruction rejects alternate request and acknowledgment bytes; both regressions passed.

Receiver cleanup could relinquish child ownership before exit and skip independent cleanup on failure. Retain ownership until observed exit, bound forced termination, aggregate cleanup failures and exercise a noncooperating child in both ideal and real acceptance.
execution: Independent wallet/transport focused suite before final regression additions
Independent immediate parent-disconnect probe: receiver exited, no surviving child
Final cleanup readback: no unresolved material findings
review.executionGate: Full local check and final ideal/real HTTPS acceptance passed.

limits: Known LocalVenue ledger and public fixture obligor keys, not authenticated external finality or real funds.
Plaintext DB/WAL/backups; no copied-database rollback protection, supported device custody or seed-only restore.

HTTPS uses public fixture TLS keys and a trusted local pairing file. Authenticated pairing/discovery, private deployed credentials and certificate lifecycle are not implemented; TLS does not hide network metadata.
Separate public-input audit is not an operating-system sandbox.
Abrupt process-exit tests do not cover power loss or storage corruption; their proof fixtures are ideal. Real acceptance separately retains actual proof bytes across process restarts.
Historical fulfillment and received records are not current-spendability assertions or exactly-once external goods/payout.
CLI currently supports one pinned segment without imports; no automatic note selection, reservation release or lapse/replacement support.
No normative changes, new circuit pins, deployment or release. This record summarizes inspected sources and observed results, not a raw transcript.

receiverBoundary.result: unspent or spent at the exact returned checkpoint, or typed unavailable/invalid; unknown local request throws UNKNOWN
checks: Stored request backing/value/owner and locally derived ownership match.
Only verified deduplicated event closure is read, including imported outputs and imported spentness.
A payment checkpoint remains unspent after a later burn checkpoint reports spent; unverified served tails do not affect status.
Missing, corrupt, mismatched, absent-note and wrong-authority evidence never reports unspent and never consumes an invoice.
Note and target bytes are owned before asynchronous proof callbacks.
CLI checks unspent before fulfillment or preparing proofs; historical fulfill remains unchanged.
fulfillment(id) restores the original opening, receipt and checkpoint across restart/crash; duplicate writes still conflict and returned-byte mutation cannot alter saved state.
limits: One caller-configured segment per handle. No newest external-state claim or assurance of present spendability.
No receipt authentication by checkNote; fulfill still authenticates the exact delivery.
Saved fulfillment is not another authorization to credit or deliver goods.

retirement.review: Bounded independent comparison found active equivalents for receiver, proof, admission, history, audit and crash cases. Framework-specific journal formats are not a product contract.
retained: Git history and immutable contract/report links

deliveryBoundary.admission: Trusted authenticated pairing binds request/domain/endpoint/CA and durable random 256-bit scoped bearer capability. Standard certificate chain/hostname verification; no redirects or TLS bypass.
deliveryBoundary.storage: Original receipt-attested statement and matching receiver opening are committed as one immutable canonical frame. Exact replay returns its SHA-256 hash; conflict refuses replacement.
deliveryBoundary.acknowledgment: Durably stored only; no proof verification, checkpoint finality, invoice fulfillment or external credit.
deliveryBoundary.schema: Two additive tables in the existing wallet database; token and inbox persist across restart.
hostileCases: otherwise valid alternate proof and altered original signature
